correctness.rationale: For any smooth quartic over F2, a collinear triple of rational hyperflexes would force the shared line restriction to vanish at all three F2 points and repeat one root, contradicting line contact 4P at a distinct point. A noncollinear triple normalizes to coordinate vertices and forces their only permitted Fano tangent lines Y+Z,X+Z,X+Y. Equal restrictions make any candidate differ from the displayed F0 by Δ·(aX+bY+cZ), but gradient at each vertex forces a=b=c=0. The displayed symmetric expansion F0=s²q+sr+q² and its factored derivatives exclude any common zero of F0 and derivatives over the algebraic closure; exactly the vertices are rational zeros. Every noncollinear unordered triple corresponds to one F0 projective image: 168 ordered bases/6 =28, stabilizer S3. Separately independently implemented all 32767 nonzero F2 ternary quartic masks and rational tangent restrictions, recovering hyperflex histogram 0:23331,1:8148,2:1260,3:28 and representative mask 15150; this matches the inspected 28-row certificate. The source verifier’s Groebner unit-ideal checks for all affine charts were inspected; the analytic smoothness proof supplies independent all-closure support.
residual_risks: Only geometrically smooth plane quartics defined over F2, rational points with contact exactly four. Does not classify ordinary flexes, Weierstrass divisors, all quartic isomorphism classes or fields > F2.
